findings.description: The wrapper's statistics dict is cleared and then shared by every call, so concurrent awaits of the same decorated function write into one dict and reset each other's statistics.
findings.rationale: Trigger: two coroutines await the same decorated function at the same time. Mechanism: each call runs stats.clear() on the shared wrapper dict and then assigns that dict to its copy's _local.statistics, so attempt_number and start_time from one call are overwritten by the other. Impact: statistics read from the wrapper (or from retry_state) are silently wrong. The original code gave each call its own copy.statistics dict, which avoided this.

findings.description: The sync wrapper clears and reuses one shared statistics dict across calls, so concurrent threads calling the same decorated function corrupt each other's statistics.
findings.rationale: Trigger: two threads call the same decorated function at once. Mechanism: stats.clear() and the shared dict assignment on lines 377-379 let both calls write to the same dict, which the original per-call copy.statistics avoided. Impact: stats such as attempt_number are interleaved or reset, giving silently wrong values.
